rule: In the informal (patio) Dominican mode, a capicúa is when a player's last tile can be placed on either end. If that last tile is a double, it is not a capicúa.
quote: Si la ficha es un doble entonces no hay capicúa.
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Dominó dominicano

rule: The player who makes the capicúa gets 25 or 30 points, depending on the agreed rules (patio mode).
quote: se le suman 25 o 30 puntos dependiendo de las reglas
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Dominó dominicano

rule: Capicúa is a 25-point bonus on the last play: the player going out plays a tile that matches the end on the opposite side of the line. The bonus can be nullified.
quote: he collects another 25 points, though this play too can also be nullified
sourceName: DR1.com, '25, 50, Capicua! Dominoes and the Dominican Republic' (page 2, Wayback 2015 copy)

rule: The capicúa bonus is nullified if the matching last tile is a blank or a double.
quote: does it with either a blank, or with a double, the points are nullified
sourceName: DR1.com, '25, 50, Capicua!' (page 2)

rule: Capicúa refers only to the last play of the hand, when the player goes out (not to a locked game).
quote: This term is in reference to the last play of the game.
sourceName: DR1.com, '25, 50, Capicua!' (page 2)

rule: A Dominican linguist (Academia Dominicana de la Lengua member) defines capicúa as when only one tile is left that closes the game and it is a 'head at both ends' (fits both ends).
quote: es “cabeza de dos extremos”, se dice que es “capicúa”
sourceName: Acento, 'Dominó' by Roberto Guzmán (2025)

rule: Capicúa is a play that goes out (domina) by either of the two ends. No point value given.
quote: Consiste en hacer una jugada para dominar por cualquiera de los dos extremos.
sourceName: Listín Diario, 'El bueno, el malo y el feo' (opinion, 2019)

rule: Winning by capicúa has special prestige: closing the game at both ends with one play.
quote: Cerrar el juego por los dos cabos en un solo tranco
sourceName: Diario Libre, 'Dominó | La república de las fichas' by Aníbal de Castro (2026)

rule: In some Dominican playing groups, a capicúa is worth double (the hand counts double) instead of a fixed bonus.
quote: En algunos corros vale doble
sourceName: Diario Libre, Aníbal de Castro (2026)

rule: Santiago municipal tournament (2019): capicúa is worth 25 tantos; the paso corrido earns nothing.
quote: NO VALE TANTOS EL PASO CORRIDO, LA CAPICUA SON 25 TANTOS.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, rules of 1er Torneo de Dominó Copa Alcaldía de Santiago (Aug 2019)

rule: La Guáyiga municipal tournament (Oct 2025): capicúa is worth +30 points.
quote: Capicúa: +30 pts.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, 'Gran Torneo de Dominó Regular 3/2' rules

rule: In the Dominican Republic, capicúa is going out with a tile that fits both ends, except when it is a double; such special plays are normally worth 25.
quote: dominar con una ficha que pueda ser colocada por ambos extremos, salvo que sea un doble

rule: FichaFlow (Dominican domino app) requires a non-double last tile that contains both distinct end values; ends 5 and 5 with the 5-5 do not count.
quote: Capicúa requires a non-double final tile containing both distinct pre-play end values.

rule: FichaFlow default capicúa bonus is 25; 30 is also a common Dominican value. Its value page cites elCaribe for 25, La Guáyiga for 30, and a Santiago tournament for 25.

rule: Restating DR1: if the last tile matches the opposite end but is not a blank or a double, the player gets 25 points.

rule: A Dominican slang dictionary defines capicúa as winning a domino game 'by the 2 ends'.

sourceName: Ser Dominicano Es Lo Máximo (slang dictionary)

rule: Puerto Rico: capicú is when the winning tile can play on either end; it does not apply when the winning tile is a double.
